memory_update.text: FORM should be carried forward as a high-priority underfollowed HBM testing candidate because its probe-card products map directly to known-good-die and HBM microbump test constraints.

KLIC should be carried forward as an underfollowed bonding-equipment hypothesis; strongest validation requires proving that TCB demand is HBM-related rather than mostly CPO or general heterogeneous integration.
ONTO should be carried forward as an advanced-packaging inspection/metrology and process-control candidate, especially for panel-level packaging, glass substrates, and yield bottlenecks.

The HBM sub-supplier chokepoint appears strongest in test/probe cards, TCB bonding tools, advanced packaging process control/metrology, and OSAT 2.5D/3D TSV capacity rather than in memory producers alone.

Need a later pass for US-listed materials/chemicals and thermal-interface suppliers; this pass found stronger public evidence for equipment/test/metrology than for pure-play underfill or thermal materials exposure.

node: HBM and advanced-packaging sub-suppliers one or two layers below memory producers
summary: Expanded a focused US-listed universe around the HBM/advanced-packaging sub-supplier node. The strongest fit for an underfollowed lane is not the memory producers themselves, but companies tied to known-good-die testing, probe cards, thermocompression bonding, advanced packaging inspection/metrology, TSV/2.5D/3D packaging services, and panel-level packaging process control. This pass keeps one reference/context OSAT name and three smaller or mid-cap supplier/equipment names. No buy/sell view is implied.
